title: Allahabad HC Rules a Mere FSSAI Registration Cannot Cover a Large-Scale Slaughterhouse
case_name: Junaid Alam v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
card_summary: A Division Bench dismissed a petition to reopen a slaughterhouse on a petty food business registration alone. The petitioner's own licence application disclosed a capacity of twenty large animals a day, beyond the petty business threshold, so the Court held a regular licence under Section 31(1) was required. GST, Udyam, lab reports and a municipal NOC could not substitute for that licence.
card_tip: Match your FSSAI paperwork to actual scale before reopening or expanding; a registration meant for a petty food business will not cover large-capacity operations.
verification_notes: Confirmed across LiveLaw, Legal Suvidha and SupremeToday, which agree on the bench (Justices Ajit Kumar and Garima Prashad), the dismissal of the petition, the disclosed 20-animal capacity, and the ancillary-documents holding. The exact date of pronouncement is not stated in any of the three reports; 13 September 2026 is LiveLaw's report date and is used here as the closest available proxy, not a confirmed decision date.
